clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 to buy an apple orchard: June became homesick and wrote daily to her sister Edna; Walter stayed out in the trees and distanced from June; Glen got into fights at school; Walter and his brother Harlan stopped speaking after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter; Walter and June rowed over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, her anxiety easing and functioning rising. The shifts fall close together across the family in the months after the move and through the following winter.

clusters.name: The orchard failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily; he and Glen blamed each other over the loan; Glen took over the family's money and talks with the bank, overfunctioning; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; you began wetting the bed in April 1969; Ida was found to have heart trouble and told to stop working. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, his functioning rising. The shifts pile up across the family from the crop loss through the auction in October and into the spring after.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: he sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard for hours, his functioning down; he and Marian had loud fights over money at night; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, overfunctioning to cover; you stopped eating properly and lost a lot of weight that summer; you kept to your room and distanced from your mother; Walter began drinking again after six years off it. By June 1976, when Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, you began eating again and made the track team, your functioning rising. The shifts fall close together from the job loss through the spring of 1976.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, distancing; Hollis took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool and was sent home twice; Wilma took over Lily's care, overfunctioning; you developed eczema flaring on both hands; you and Hollis had rows most nights. By June 1991, when Wilma took a flat in town, your eczema cleared over the summer. The shifts fall close together from Wilma's arrival through the spring of 1991, and her move out settles the period.
